item.title: Sakura Shrimp: Suruga Bay's Pink Treasure — Guide
item.description: Sakura shrimp (sakura-ebi) are tiny, translucent deep-water shrimp with a delicate pink colour like cherry blossom, caught commercially nowhere in Japan but the deep waters of Suruga Bay, making them one of the country’s most localised delicacies. The fishing seasons run in spring and autumn from the port of Yui, whose restaurants serve the catch raw over rice, fried into crisp golden kakiage fritters, or dried, and in season the drying yards spread the shrimp in pink carpets against a backdrop of Mount Fuji.
